name: TeamStarWolf - Notepad++ Update-Channel Hijack CVE-2025-15556 Case Study
description: Curated case-study layer, not an official MITRE mapping. ATT&CK techniques that the verified record of the 2025 Notepad++ update-channel hijack (CVE-2025-15556) supports: the Notepad++ posts, the CVE, NVD and KEV records, and Reported research from Rapid7 and Kaspersky. Each comment names source numbers from case-studies/NOTEPAD_PLUS_PLUS_UPDATE_HIJACK_2026.md. Scores: 75 the vendor, CVE or KEV record describes the behavior; 50 vendor research describes it. Rapid7's published ids are bound to ATT&CK v20.0 (T1574.002 maps to T1574.001); T1195.002 is this study's mapping.

legendItems.label: 75: described in the vendor, CVE or KEV record

metadata.name: score_meaning
metadata.value: 75 = the vendor, CVE or KEV record describes the behavior; 50 = vendor research (Rapid7, Kaspersky) describes it. No severity, prevalence or coverage is measured.

metadata.value: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise v20.0: technique IDs and tactics normalized to data/attack/technique_profiles.jsonl by scripts/build_navigator_layers.py

techniques.comment: Compromise Software Supply Chain: delivery through the hijacked Notepad++ update channel: selected users' update traffic redirected to serve compromised updates, June to December 2025 (vendor, 2 Feb 2026) [1]; CVE-2025-15556 (3 Feb 2026) [10]. This study's mapping; Rapid7 does not list it. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/NOTEPAD_PLUS_PLUS_UPDATE_HIJACK_2026.md.

Malicious File: malicious update installer run after Notepad++ and its updater (Rapid7, 2 Feb 2026) [14]; update file launched by the updater in all three Kaspersky chains (3 Feb 2026) [15]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/NOTEPAD_PLUS_PLUS_UPDATE_HIJACK_2026.md.

Masquerading: renamed Bitdefender Submission Wizard used as the sideloading host; listed by Rapid7 for the Chrysalis chain (2 Feb 2026, updated 9 Feb; activity June to November 2025) [14]. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/NOTEPAD_PLUS_PLUS_UPDATE_HIJACK_2026.md.

DLL: DLL sideloading to the Chrysalis backdoor (Rapid7) [14] and Kaspersky chain 3, October 2025 [15]. Rapid7 lists the revoked T1574.002, which data/attack/superseded_by.jsonl maps here. Source numbers refer to the Sources table of case-studies/NOTEPAD_PLUS_PLUS_UPDATE_HIJACK_2026.md.
